common_name: Double-Comb Indomalayan Fly (Paired Oblique Tarsal Sex-Comb Rows)

equations.activator: du/dt = D_u lap(u) + gamma * (a - u + u^2 v)
equations.inhibitor: dv/dt = D_v lap(v) + gamma * (b - u^2 v)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = largest eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
equations.chronoseries_scaling: lambda / lambda_focal = sqrt(D_u / D_u_focal) at fixed gamma and delta

state_variables.u: membrane-tethered melanin-precursor activator on the 1.92 µm ocellar/tergite pigment field

boundary_conditions.domain: periodic 15.36 µm × 15.36 µm square (exactly 8 focal linear wavelengths)
boundary_conditions.note: No-flux anatomy is not claimed; the patch is an interior periodic sample of cuticle.

parameters.note: gamma is computed in the script so that the continuous k_c of the focal species is exactly 2π/1.92 µm. It is not copied from the 86 µm sibling slot.

reported: Turing 1952: a coupled reaction-diffusion system can select a finite critical wavenumber.
Schnakenberg 1979: the cubic kinetics a-u+u^2 v, b-u^2 v.
Kopp & True 2002 and Mishra & Singh 2006: D. bipectinata carries paired oblique sex-comb rows, distinct from neighbouring Sophophora.
Gompel et al. 2005: D. biarmipes wing pigment is a gain of a spot, the predecessor contrast at the organ scale.
reconstructed: Focal linear wavelength is set to the assigned 1.92 µm rung by solving for gamma.
Predecessor and successor wavelengths 2.40 µm and 1.536 µm follow from Du factors 25/16 and 16/25 at the same gamma and diffusion ratio, at geological age 0 Ma for all three.
does_not_claim: That Kopp or Mishra measured 1.92 µm.
That D. biarmipes and D. buzzatii are stratigraphic ancestors of D. bipectinata.
That the gallery JPEG is a micrograph of the 1.92 µm field.
